issues.t: Head gasket leaks oil or coolant
issues.sym: Oil seeping from between the engine block and cylinder head, coolant loss, oil smoke, overheating or loss of power. Some owners report the gasket failing again after replacement.
issues.why: The head gasket on these four-cylinder engines is the most reported Breeze problem, often between 40,000 and 75,000 miles. Cam seals and spark plug tube seals often leak at the same time.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and oil and coolant levels. If it overheats, pull over and shut it off. Get a compression or leak-down test; a head gasket job done before the engine overheats badly costs far less than an engine.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure or stuck in one gear
issues.sym: Shifts become erratic, the car lurches or gets stuck in a single gear and won't accelerate normally, or the transmission stops working.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic fails from internal wear or from electrical parts such as its speed sensors and solenoids. When it detects a fault it locks itself into one gear to protect itself.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and use only the correct Chrysler-spec fluid. If it is stuck in one gear, drive slowly to a shop and have the transmission codes read; a sensor fault is much cheaper than a rebuild.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and start an engine fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking onto the engine, smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, often shortly after parking.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose can crack and spray fluid onto hot engine parts. Owners report fires, some of them total losses, and Chrysler recalled the cars to replace the hose.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, shut off the engine, get everyone out and stay away. Ask a Chrysler dealer whether recall 06V001 was done, and have any leaking hose replaced right away.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks if not replaced on schedule
issues.sym: The engine quits suddenly while driving and then cranks with an even, fast sound, as if it has no compression.
issues.why: Both engines use a rubber timing belt that wears with age and mileage. When it snaps the engine stops, and valves can be bent, which raises the repair bill.
issues.next: If the engine dies and cranks unusually fast, don't keep cranking it; have it towed. If you don't know when the belt was last changed, replace it with the water pump and tensioner as preventive maintenance.

issues.t: Misfire from leaking spark plug tube seals
issues.sym: The engine shakes or runs rough, the check engine light flashes or stays on, fuel economy drops, and oil may be found on the spark plugs.
issues.why: Seals around the spark plug tubes in the valve cover harden and let oil into the spark plug wells, which shorts out the plugs.
issues.next: Have the plugs pulled and checked for oil. Replacing the tube seals, valve cover gasket and fouled plugs usually cures the misfire. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Stalling when warm or won't start
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning once warmed up, at any speed, and may be hard to restart. Some owners report a no-start after the car sits.
issues.why: Owners report stalling and no-starts across these years. Causes vary, including fuel delivery, sensors and wiring, so it needs testing while it happens.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer firmly to safety and press the brake hard. Have a shop scan for codes and check fuel pressure and the crank sensor while the problem is present.

issues.t: Brakes pull left, wear fast or pulse
issues.sym: The car pulls to the left when braking, brake parts wear out early, or the pedal pulses from warped rotors.
issues.why: A brake line routed near the exhaust lets the brake fluid get too hot, causing pulling and early wear. Rotor problems are also among the most reported brake complaints.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected, including line routing near the exhaust, and replace worn pads and rotors. Don't ignore a strong pull; it can upset the car in a hard stop.

issues.t: Clunk or rattle in the steering from a loose shaft bolt
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle felt through the steering wheel, especially over bumps or when turning.
issues.why: The pinch bolt on the steering shaft coupling works loose.
issues.next: Have a shop check and tighten the coupling bolt soon; loose steering parts should not be left alone.

issues.t: Power steering moan or whine
issues.sym: The power steering moans or whines, either when cold or once warmed up.
issues.why: Cold-weather noise can come from the fluid and may go away with a fluid change. A moan when warm on 1996-1997 cars needs a new high-pressure hose.
issues.next: Check the fluid level first. If the noise remains, have the hose and pump inspected, and watch for leaks.

issues.t: Popping in the front end from worn tie rods
issues.sym: Popping or clunking from the front, felt through the steering wheel and floor.
issues.why: The tie rod ends wear out and need replacing.
issues.next: Have the tie rods checked and replaced, then get an alignment. Worn tie rods make steering loose and wear tires quickly.

issues.t: Lower ball joint can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end. In the worst case the ball joint separates and the wheel collapses, causing loss of steering.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints could lose lubrication and wear until they separate. Chrysler recalled the cars, and ball joint and lower arm complaints are common.
issues.next: Ask a Chrysler dealer whether recall 97V201 was done. Any clunk from the front end should be checked before highway driving.

issues.t: Some aftermarket ball joints and control arms can separate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before failure. Applies only if the front ball joints or control arms were replaced with certain aftermarket parts.
issues.why: Two aftermarket parts recalls covered replacement ball joints and control arms whose ball studs could pull out, letting the wheel fold under.
issues.next: If your front suspension has been rebuilt, ask the shop which brand was used. Affected parts are replaced free by the part maker.

issues.t: Some replacement fuel pumps can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power or stalling. Applies only if the fuel pump was replaced with certain aftermarket pumps.
issues.why: Aftermarket fuel pumps and pump modules covered by parts-maker recalls could restrict fuel flow.
issues.next: If the fuel pump has been replaced and the car stalls or loses power, ask the shop which brand was used and have it checked.

issues.t: Some replacement fuel filters can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or drips under the car. Applies only if the fuel filter was replaced with certain aftermarket filters.
issues.why: An aftermarket fuel filter recall covered filters that could leak and cause a fire.
issues.next: If you smell gas, don't drive. Have the filter brand and fuel lines checked.

issues.t: Car can roll away after shifting to Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key may come out when the shifter isn't fully in Park, or the car moves after being parked.
issues.why: Problems with the ignition-park interlock and shifter could let the car roll away without warning. Owners report crashes from this.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Ask a Chrysler dealer whether recall 04V021 was done.

issues.t: Key-shift interlock can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: You can take the key out without the shifter in Park.
issues.why: A misadjusted cable or a broken pin in the shift button could disable the ignition-park interlock on automatic cars.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and confirm the car is in Park. Ask a dealer whether recall 98V183 was done.

issues.t: Rear brake line can rub and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near the right rear, a lower or softer pedal, and longer stops.
issues.why: The right rear brake tube could rub against an exhaust clamp until it leaked, cutting braking on half of the system.
issues.next: If the pedal feels soft, stop driving and have it towed. Ask a dealer whether recall 99V244 was done.

issues.t: Front brake line bracket can break (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak at the right front and a soft pedal.
issues.why: A poorly welded bracket could let the right front brake tube fatigue and crack, losing half the braking system.
issues.next: If the pedal sinks or feels soft, stop driving. Ask a dealer whether recall 00V196 was done.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak (recall)
issues.sym: The brake warning light comes on and the pedal goes lower or feels softer.
issues.why: The master cylinder could leak fluid and weaken one half of the split brake system.
issues.next: If the brake light comes on, check the fluid and have it inspected before driving further. Ask a dealer whether recall 96V075 was done.

issues.t: ABS valve can stick and make the car pull (recall)
issues.sym: The car swerves or pulls to one side during a straight stop.
issues.why: Corrosion in the ABS hydraulic unit could make a front valve stick.
issues.next: If the car pulls hard when braking, have it inspected right away. Ask a dealer whether recall 96V074 was done.

issues.t: Hood may not stay latched (recall)
issues.sym: The hood may not be held by the safety catch if it isn't fully latched.
issues.why: The secondary hood latch spring could come loose if the hood was slammed.
issues.next: Check the hood is fully closed before driving. Ask a dealer whether recall 97V095 was done.

issues.t: Child seat tether instructions missing (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The owner's manual may leave out how to attach a child seat tether strap.
issues.why: Without the right instructions a child seat might not be anchored properly in a crash.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the corrected information under recall 00V366 and follow the child seat maker's instructions.

issues.t: Fuel tank straps may be unpainted and rust (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom at first. Unprotected straps can rust and loosen over time.
issues.why: A few cars were built with fuel tank straps missing their protective paint.
issues.next: Have the straps inspected for rust when the car is on a lift, and ask a dealer about recall 00V067.

issues.t: Rusted fuel filler tube can break
issues.sym: Gasoline pours out under the car while filling up, or the filler tube hangs loose.
issues.why: The metal tube from the gas cap to the tank can rust through in older cars.
issues.next: If fuel leaks during a fill-up, stop pumping and keep away from flames. Have the filler tube replaced before driving.

issues.t: Rough running at start-up and high emissions
issues.sym: Poor drivability right after starting and possibly failed emissions tests.
issues.why: An engine computer calibration problem; updating or replacing the computer fixed it, possibly under the emissions warranty.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check for an engine computer update and scan for codes.

issues.t: Horn sounds by itself when turning
issues.sym: The horn honks on its own when you turn the steering wheel.
issues.why: A worn horn contact or clockspring in the steering column shorts as the wheel turns.
issues.next: Pull the horn fuse as a short-term fix and have the steering column wiring checked. Airbag parts are nearby, so leave this to a shop.

issues.t: Radiator failure
issues.sym: Coolant leaks from the radiator, and the engine may run hot.
issues.why: The radiator cracks or leaks with age.
issues.next: Keep coolant topped up and watch the temperature gauge. Replace the radiator before the engine overheats, since overheating can blow the head gasket.

issues.t: Weak keyless entry range
issues.sym: The remote only locks or unlocks the doors from very close.
issues.why: The keyless entry receiver antenna is weak and needs replacing.
issues.next: Try a fresh remote battery first. If range is still poor, a shop can replace the receiver antenna.

issues.t: Water leaks in through the doors
issues.sym: Wet carpet or water inside the doors after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The plastic water shields behind the door panels don't seal properly.
issues.next: Have the door panels removed and the shields resealed. Dry the carpet to stop mold and rust.
